Bank hash comparison state, locking, insert, and stake-based mismatch checks.

# Purpose
This C file implements the runtime logic for a bank hash comparison object, `fd_bank_hash_cmp`. It provides the object life cycle functions [`fd_bank_hash_cmp_new`](<#fd_bank_hash_cmp_new>), [`fd_bank_hash_cmp_join`](<#fd_bank_hash_cmp_join>), [`fd_bank_hash_cmp_leave`](<#fd_bank_hash_cmp_leave>), and [`fd_bank_hash_cmp_delete`](<#fd_bank_hash_cmp_delete>), which manage an instance stored in caller supplied memory. The code checks for `NULL` pointers and alignment, clears the memory during creation, sets the internal map offset, and verifies the final footprint. It also provides [`fd_bank_hash_cmp_lock`](<#fd_bank_hash_cmp_lock>) and [`fd_bank_hash_cmp_unlock`](<#fd_bank_hash_cmp_unlock>) for mutual exclusion, using an atomic compare and swap when thread support is enabled.

The main work happens in [`fd_bank_hash_cmp_insert`](<#fd_bank_hash_cmp_insert>) and [`fd_bank_hash_cmp_check`](<#fd_bank_hash_cmp_check>). [`fd_bank_hash_cmp_insert`](<#fd_bank_hash_cmp_insert>) records the local bank hash in `ours` or stores remote hashes in `theirs` with their stake values, grouped by slot in an internal map. It also handles duplicate hashes, stake accumulation, map overflow, and removal of old entries below the watermark. [`fd_bank_hash_cmp_check`](<#fd_bank_hash_cmp_check>) compares the local hash against the hash with the highest stake for a slot, and reports a match or mismatch when the winning stake is above 52 percent of total stake. When a mismatch is found, the code logs the slot, both hashes, and the stake share, then removes the entry from the map.
